1	Benchmark contamination is widely assumed to inflate language model scores, yet its actual effect has never been systematically measured across model families. We perform controlled SFT injection at five dosage levels into six models spanning five independent families (7B--14.7B) and discover a spectrum of dose-response patterns, not uniform inflation. Two patterns replicate across independent families: Immune (Phi-4, LLaMA-3.1) and Benefit (statistically significant for Gemma-2, BCa 95\% CI [$+$1.49, $+$3.14]\,pp; directionally consistent for Falcon3; borderline for OLMo-2). Two more extreme patterns---Collapse and V-recovery---are each observed in one family (Qwen2.5) across three seeds but await independent replication. A volume-matched control decomposes Benefit into 45\% data quantity and 55\% contamination content; Collapse and Immune cannot arise from volume effects alone. Effects are benchmark-conditional: MMLU-targeted contamination improves GSM8K in five of six families, even those harmed on MMLU, consistent with capability elicitation rather than item memorization. Difference-in-differences analysis detects no item-specific memorization at current power levels. We characterize detection signal failure: Min-K\%++ exhibits directional reversal at small scales (paired Cohen's $d = -1.98$). ContamCal, our diagnostic framework combining multi-signal exposure mapping with contamination-augmented IRT, enables domain-level contamination diagnosis with credible intervals. Out-of-sample validation on LLaMA-3.1-8B confirms Immune despite matching a Benefit family's baseline, demonstrating that model family characteristics beyond baseline ability modulate vulnerability. Model-specific dose-response profiling is necessary for reliable benchmark interpretation.

tool_args.old_string: Benchmark contamination is widely assumed to inflate language model scores, yet its actual effect has never been systematically measured across model families. We perform controlled SFT injection at five dosage levels into six models spanning five independent families (7B--14.7B) and discover a spectrum of dose-response patterns, not uniform inflation. Two patterns replicate across independent families: Immune (Phi-4, LLaMA-3.1) and Benefit (statistically significant for Gemma-2, BCa 95\% CI [$+$1.49, $+$3.14]\,pp; directionally consistent for Falcon3; borderline for OLMo-2). Two more extreme patterns---Collapse and V-recovery---are each observed in one family (Qwen2.5) across three seeds but await independent replication. A volume-matched control decomposes Benefit into 45\% data quantity and 55\% contamination content; Collapse and Immune cannot arise from volume effects alone. Effects are benchmark-conditional: MMLU-targeted contamination improves GSM8K in five of six families, even those harmed on MMLU, consistent with capability elicitation rather than item memorization. Difference-in-differences analysis detects no item-specific memorization at current power levels. We characterize detection signal failure: Min-K\%++ exhibits directional reversal at small scales (paired Cohen's $d = -1.98$). ContamCal, our diagnostic framework combining multi-signal exposure mapping with contamination-augmented IRT, enables domain-level contamination diagnosis with credible intervals. Out-of-sample validation on LLaMA-3.1-8B confirms Immune despite matching a Benefit family's baseline, demonstrating that model family characteristics beyond baseline ability modulate vulnerability. Model-specific dose-response profiling is necessary for reliable benchmark interpretation.
tool_args.new_string: Benchmark contamination is widely assumed to inflate language model scores, yet its actual effect has never been systematically measured across model families. We perform controlled SFT injection at five dosage levels into six models (7B--14.7B) from five open-source families and discover a spectrum of dose-response patterns, not uniform inflation. Two patterns replicate across independent families: Immune (Phi-4, LLaMA-3.1) and Benefit (statistically significant for Gemma-2, BCa 95\% CI [$+$1.49, $+$3.14]\,pp; borderline for OLMo-2 and Falcon3). Collapse and V-recovery are each observed in one family (Qwen2.5) across three seeds but remain preliminary pending independent replication. Effects are benchmark-conditional: MMLU-targeted contamination improves GSM8K in five of six families, even those harmed on MMLU. Difference-in-differences analysis detects no item-specific memorization; a volume-matched control attributes 45\% of Benefit to data quantity. ContamCal, our diagnostic framework combining multi-signal exposure mapping with contamination-augmented IRT, enables domain-level contamination diagnosis with credible intervals---revealing that Social Sciences contamination effects are negative while STEM effects are positive, a pattern invisible to aggregate scoring. Out-of-sample validation on LLaMA-3.1-8B confirms that model family characteristics beyond baseline ability modulate vulnerability. Model-specific dose-response profiling is necessary for reliable benchmark interpretation.

\paragraph{Contamination vs.\ additional training.}
The volume-matched control (\S\ref{sec:memorization_test}) decomposes Benefit into ${\sim}$45\% data quantity and ${\sim}$55\% contamination content. Whether this distinction is meaningful is clarified by the non-Benefit patterns: non-benchmark MCQ data does not produce Collapse ($-$9.4pp) or model-specific divergence, indicating benchmark-specific content triggers qualitatively different responses than generic MCQ training.
tool_args.new_string:
\paragraph{Contamination vs.\ additional training.}
SFT injection simultaneously introduces three confounded signals: contamination content, additional training volume ($+$33\% at d100), and LoRA parameter updates. The volume-matched control (\S\ref{sec:memorization_test}) decomposes Falcon3's Benefit into ${\sim}$45\% data quantity and ${\sim}$55\% contamination content; this decomposition is available only for Falcon3 and may not generalize. The non-Benefit patterns provide complementary evidence: non-benchmark MCQ data does not produce Collapse ($-$9.4pp) or model-specific divergence, indicating benchmark-specific content triggers qualitatively different responses than generic MCQ training.
